questions.stem: What does the phase of a wave determine?
choices: The maximum displacement of the wave
The time period of the wave
The displacement of the wave at any position and instant
The distance between two consecutive crests
questions.solution: The phase of a wave determines the displacement of the wave at any position and instant because it represents the state of the wave at a specific point in space and time. The maximum displacement is determined by the amplitude, the time period is related to the frequency, and the distance between two consecutive crests is the wavelength.

questions.stem: How does the crest of a wave progress with time?
choices: It remains stationary
It moves in the negative direction of x-axis
It moves in the positive direction of x-axis
It oscillates randomly
questions.solution: The crest of a wave progresses in the positive direction of the x-axis with time because the wave's motion is defined by the phase of the wave equation, which requires the crest to move forward as time increases. The other options are incorrect because a stationary crest would imply no wave motion, a negative direction would contradict the wave's propagation, and random oscillation would not follow the regular pattern of a wave.

questions.stem: If a wave is propagating through a medium, what does the wavefront represent?
choices: The direction of the wave
The energy carried by the wave
The locus of points with the same phase
The frequency of the wave
questions.solution: A wavefront represents the locus of points that are in the same phase of their oscillation. This is because wavefronts show where the wave is at the same point in its cycle across space. The other options do not accurately describe what a wavefront represents.

questions.stem: Which of the following can be concluded about the propagation of waves in a medium?
choices: Only transverse waves can propagate in all media.
Only longitudinal waves can propagate in all media.
Both transverse and longitudinal waves can propagate in solids.
Only surface waves can propagate in liquids.
questions.solution: Solids have the necessary rigidity to support both transverse and longitudinal waves, as transverse waves involve particle motion perpendicular to the wave direction, and longitudinal waves involve particle motion parallel to the wave direction. Fluids lack the shear strength required for transverse waves, so they only support longitudinal waves. The other options are incorrect because not all media support only one type of wave, and surface waves are not the only type that can exist in liquids.

hi.stem: एक माध्यम में तरंगों के प्रसार के बारे में निम्नलिखित में से क्या निष्कर्ष निकाला जा सकता है?
choices: सभी माध्यमों में केवल अनुप्रस्थ तरंगें ही प्रसारित हो सकती हैं।
सभी माध्यमों में केवल अनुदैर्ध्य तरंगें ही प्रसारित हो सकती हैं।
ठोस में अनुप्रस्थ और अनुदैर्ध्य दोनों प्रकार की तरंगें प्रसारित हो सकती हैं।
तरल में केवल सतही तरंगें ही प्रसारित हो सकती हैं।
hi.solution: ठोस में अनुप्रस्थ तरंगों के लिए आवश्यक कठोरता होती है, जबकि अनुदैर्ध्य तरंगों के लिए आवश्यकता नहीं होती। अनुप्रस्थ तरंगों में कणों का गति तरंग की दिशा के लंबवत होता है, जबकि अनुदैर्ध्य तरंगों में कणों का गति तरंग की दिशा के समांतर होता है। द्रव अनुप्रस्थ तरंगों के लिए आवश्यक अपरूपण शक्ति नहीं रखते हैं, इसलिए वे केवल अनुदैर्ध्य तरंगों को ही समर्थन करते हैं। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं क्योंकि सभी माध्यम एक ही प्रकार की तरंग को समर्थन नहीं करते हैं, और तरल में केवल सतही तरंगें ही अस्तित्व में हो सकती हैं यह सही नहीं है।
